nuggets.title: FIFO GPU Queue Blocks Premium Users During Viral Trend

scenario.symptoms: Paid tier p99 time-to-first-pixel exceeds 8 minutes during a viral prompt trend. Free tier jobs dominate the single FIFO GPU queue.
scenario.interviewerSetup: All diffusion jobs share one global queue processed strictly first-in-first-out without priority classes or preemption.

incident.headline: Single FIFO scheduler starves paid users when free-tier demand spikes

agenda.goal: Schedule GPU jobs with priority queues, reserved capacity, and fair sharing across tiers.
agenda.opener: Paying customers waited eight minutes for images while free traffic spiked. How do you schedule diffusion jobs on limited GPUs?

evidence.strong: Multi-level priority queues, reserved GPU pools per tier, weighted fair queuing, autoscale GPU nodes, deadline-aware scheduling.
evidence.adequate: Separate queue for paid without reserved GPUs.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes adding GPUs alone fixes fairness.
misconceptions.challenge: If free jobs fill the queue first, when does paid work start?

probes: How much GPU capacity is reserved for paid?
Can long free jobs be preempted?
hints: Priority without reserved capacity still starves.
Scale workers separately from queue policy.
agenda.referenceFix: Tiered queues with guaranteed paid capacity, WFQ across tenants.

nuggets.title: Adversarial Prompts Bypass Image Safety Filter

scenario.symptoms: Trust & safety flags 200 generated images in an hour containing disallowed content. Prompts use unicode homoglyphs and split banned tokens across languages.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Safety runs only on raw user prompt string before diffusion; no post-generation vision classifier on outputs.

incident.headline: Prompt-only moderation misses adversarial inputs and unsafe generated pixels

agenda.goal: Layer text and image safety with normalization, blocklists, classifier on output, and human review queue.
agenda.opener: Users bypassed our filter with typo prompts and still got banned imagery. How do you keep text-to-image generation safe?

evidence.strong: Prompt normalization, multi-model text safety, post-gen vision classifier, block known unsafe embeddings, rate limits, audit trail, human escalation.
evidence.adequate: Text filter only with static blocklist.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes checking the prompt text is sufficient.
misconceptions.challenge: Can diffusion produce unsafe content from an innocent-looking prompt?

probes: What runs after the image is generated?
How do you handle adversarial unicode?
hints: Defense in depth: input and output.
agenda.referenceFix: Text + image classifiers, homoglyph normalization, quarantine pipeline.

nuggets.title: GPU Autoscale Lag Leaves Queue Depth Exploding

scenario.symptoms: Queue depth hits 400k jobs during marketing launch. New GPU nodes take 12 minutes to provision while users see multi-hour waits.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Autoscaler watches queue depth but cloud GPU capacity is limited in region; scale-up is slow and there is no admission control.

incident.headline: Unbounded enqueue with slow GPU scale-up collapses user-visible capacity

agenda.goal: Match ingress to GPU capacity with admission control, pre-warmed pools, and cross-region overflow.
agenda.opener: Marketing sent traffic faster than we could add GPUs and the queue never recovered. How do you plan capacity for spiky image generation?

evidence.strong: Queue depth limits with 429/backpressure, pre-warmed GPU baseline, multi-region pools, estimated wait time, tier-based admission, cache popular prompts.
evidence.weak: Accept all jobs regardless of queue.

misconceptions.challenge: What happens in minute 1-10 of a spike while GPUs boot?

probes: When do you reject new jobs?
agenda.referenceFix: Admission when queue > threshold, pre-scaled pools for launches, regional failover.

nuggets.title: Strict Priority Inverts So Low-Priority Jobs Never Run

scenario.symptoms: Background thumbnail jobs age over 24 hours while interactive requests keep arriving. Batch SLA missed for a week during sustained traffic.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Scheduler always picks highest priority queue; continuous interactive load prevents draining lower queues entirely.

incident.headline: Strict priority scheduling starves batch tier under continuous higher-priority load

agenda.goal: Use weighted fair queuing or capped priority bands so lower tiers make progress.
agenda.opener: Batch thumbnails haven't run in days because interactive traffic never stops. How do priority classes share GPUs?

evidence.strong: WFQ across classes, reserved minimum bandwidth for batch, aging boost for old jobs, separate pools for batch vs interactive.
evidence.adequate: Two queues but strict priority always.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes strict priority always matches business intent.
misconceptions.challenge: If interactive jobs arrive constantly, when does batch run?

probes: What minimum share should batch get?
When does priority increase with wait time?
agenda.referenceFix: WFQ with batch minimum 20%, priority aging after 30m wait.

nuggets.title: Default Path Uses Largest Model for Simple Icons

scenario.symptoms: Simple 256px icon requests take 45s and cost 12x more than necessary. Product analytics show 70% of prompts are short and low resolution.
scenario.interviewerSetup: API routes all jobs to SDXL full pipeline with 50 steps regardless of requested size or complexity score.

incident.headline: One-size-fits-all model path wastes GPU time on simple low-res generation requests

agenda.goal: Route jobs to appropriate model, step count, and resolution based on request attributes and quality targets.
agenda.opener: Small icon requests take as long as poster-sized art because everything hits SDXL. How do you make generation fast for simple jobs?

evidence.strong: Router using resolution, step budget, prompt complexity, distilled models for previews, progressive refinement optional, cache common sizes.
evidence.adequate: Manual model picker in API only.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes only more GPUs improve latency.
misconceptions.challenge: Could a smaller model meet quality for 256px icons?

probes: How do you validate router decisions?
agenda.referenceFix: Tiered models with automatic routing, lower steps for drafts, upscale optional.
